items.title: Shilin Residence Chrysanthemum Show
items.hours: 2026 show "菊映方圓" runs Nov 27–Dec 13; outdoor exhibition areas 8:00 AM–7:00 PM, so it is open at 8:40 AM on Tue Dec 1. The park itself is open daily year-round 8 AM–6 PM. 2026 indoor-hall hours not yet published (2025: 8:30 AM–5 PM).
items.cost: Park and outdoor show: free (no 2026 admission fee announced). The Main Residence building (正館) is separately ticketed, open Tue–Sun 9:30–12:00 and 13:30–17:00.
items.getThere: MRT Red Line to Shilin Station Exit 2, turn left, cross Zhongshan N. Rd, ~10 min walk (Parks Office directions). Venue: Shilin Residence Park, 60 Fulin Rd (福林路60號).
highlights: Theme 菊映方圓: circles, squares and geometric lines worked into flower beds and landscape pieces across 15 themed zones.
Living plant wall designed by green-sculpture artist Lai Wen-bin (26 years' experience), inspired by Henri Matisse, co-planted with Shilin Elementary pupils.
Classic cultivation forms: large standing chrysanthemum (大立菊), cascade (懸崖菊), topiary (造型菊), large and small blooms plus daisy-family bedding.
tips: Outdoor zones open at 8 AM, so a weekday 8:40 visit beats the crowds; 35 minutes covers the outdoor loop.
Shoot the whole geometric layout from a distance first, then close-ups; the show is designed for both views.
Arts events are scheduled on weekends/holidays, so expect a quiet show on a Tuesday.
items.watch: Bloom condition depends on weather and maintenance; zones may be re-routed in rain or wind. Do not step into beds or touch displays. The workshop series was lottery-only (registration closed Oct 31).

items.title: Taxi to Lengshuikeng
items.hours: Lengshuikeng Visitor Center: 9:00 AM–4:30 PM; closed the last Monday of each month (Tue Dec 1 is open).
items.cost: Taipei taxi meter (day): NT$85 for the first 1.25 km, then NT$5 per 200 m; NT$5 per 60 s when below 5 km/h.
items.getThere: Taxi to 冷水坑遊客服務站 (台北市士林區菁山路101巷170號). Public-transport fallback: bus 小15 from MRT Jiantan toward Qingtiangang runs via Lengshuikeng; or Red 5 to Yangmingshan terminal, then the 108 park loop to the 冷水坑服務站 stop.
highlights: Lengshuikeng is a basin between Qixing and Qigu mountains, an old sulphur-mining site.
Milk Lake (牛奶湖): a milky-white pool in the Lengshuikeng explosion crater, seen from a viewing platform on a hillock on the way to the suspension bridge.
Jingshan Suspension Bridge crosses the Lengshuikeng stream, headwater of the Juansi Waterfall.
tips: YMSNP runs a live camera at the Lengshuikeng parking lot; check it for fog before leaving Shilin.
108 loop on weekdays: 07:00–17:30, every 30–40 min — fine as a fallback, too slow to rely on for timed plans.
items.watch: Xiaoyoukeng trailhead → Qixing Main Peak (~1.6 km) is fully closed Oct 27, 2026–Jan 19, 2027 (undermined footing ~560 m from Xiaoyoukeng). YMSNP names Lengshuikeng, Menghuan Lake car park and Miaopu as alternative trailheads.

items.title: Qixing Mountain: Lengshuikeng → East Peak → Main Peak → Lengshuikeng
items.hours: Trail has no gate hours; visitor centers (water, info) 9:00 AM–4:30 PM.
items.getThere: Start at the Lengshuikeng Visitor Center trailhead. Official figures: Xiaoyoukeng→Lengshuikeng 3.7 km / ~2.5 h, of which Xiaoyoukeng→Main Peak 1.65 km and Main↔East Peak 0.3 km (~15 min). So Lengshuikeng→East Peak ≈1.75 km; out-and-back to the Main Peak ≈4.1 km.
highlights: Main Peak ~1,120 m: the highest summit in Yangmingshan National Park.
The name comes from seven igneous-rock knobs left around the old crater after violent eruptions.
East Peak and Main Peak are linked by a 0.3 km saddle walk with up-and-down steps.
tips: YMSNP rates the Qixing Main–East Peak trail Grade 2; route junctions are signposted, and the closure notice advises returning the way you came.
Allow the planned 3–3.5 h: ~4.1 km round trip with sustained climbing; turn around by a fixed time to make the ~1:15 PM pickup.
items.watch: Do not continue from the Main Peak toward Xiaoyoukeng: that 1.6 km section is closed until Jan 19, 2027. Summit is exposed; cancel in fog or high wind.

items.title: Pre-Arranged Pickup at Lengshuikeng → Beitou
items.cost: Taxi meter (day): NT$85 first 1.25 km, NT$5 per 200 m, NT$5 per 60 s in slow traffic.
items.getThere: Pre-booked taxi from 冷水坑遊客服務站 to Beitou Thermal Valley (地熱谷, 中山路), about 35–40 minutes. Bus fallback (slow): the 108 loop to the Yangmingshan terminal (weekday every 30–40 minutes, last 17:30), then bus 230 down to MRT Beitou.
tips: Give the driver both the pickup point and 幽雅路30號 in Chinese when booking.
If the taxi fails, the bus fallback is slow: skip Thermal Valley and go straight on to Tamsui.

items.title: Taxi to Tamsui
items.getThere: Taxi from Xinbeitou MRT straight to Tamsui Old Street, about 30–40 minutes. MRT alternative: Xinbeitou → Beitou on the branch line (3–4 min), then the Red Line north to Tamsui (the terminus).
tips: On weekdays some Red Line trains run Beitou–Da'an only and start at Beitou heading south; for Tamsui board the northbound platform.
Taxi meter: NT$85 first 1.25 km, NT$5 per 200 m (day rate).

items.title: Tamsui — Old Street, Riverfront & Sunset
items.hours: Old Street is an open street (listed 24 h). Sunset Tue Dec 1: 5:03 PM; civil dusk ends 5:28 PM (Taipei).
items.getThere: From MRT Tamsui Station exit, turn right: Zhongzheng Rd and its extensions Chongjian St and Qingshui St form Tamsui Old Street.
highlights: Riverside sunset over the Tamsui River mouth; Taipei Travel notes the far end of Old Street opens toward Fisherman's Wharf, a classic sunset spot.
Old Street mixes traditional pastry shops and grocers with snack stalls, clothing and toy shops.
Ferry docks for Bali are along the waterfront (skip per plan).
tips: Be on the riverbank by ~4:50 PM; the best colour runs from the 5:03 sunset to ~5:28 PM dusk.
Walk the waterfront at sunset, then do Old Street and a sit-down dinner after dark.

items.title: Red Line South to Jiantan
items.getThere: Red Line from Tamsui (terminus) southbound to Jiantan; weekday trains ~6 min apart until 19:30, then ~8–10 min. Leave Jiantan by Exit 1 and walk north ~400 m to the Yangming Theater / Shilin Market area.
tips: Tamsui is the terminus, so every southbound train there passes Jiantan.
The full Tamsui–Guangci run takes ~61 min; Jiantan is well short of that.

items.title: Shilin Night Market — Games & Food
items.hours: 5:00 PM–midnight daily; no market closing day (Taipei Market Office). Individual stalls take their own rest days.
items.cost: No entry fee; each stall charges separately.
items.getThere: MRT Red Line Jiantan Station. Exit 1 is closest; walk ~400 m north to Yangming Theater and Shilin Market (101 Jihe Rd).
highlights: Taipei's largest night market: a triangle around the heritage Shilin Public Market, bounded by Wenlin Rd (east), Jihe Rd (west) and Xiaobei/Xiaoxi St (north).
Two zones: streets around Yangming Theater up to Cixian Temple on Danan Rd, and the Shilin Market building at 101 Jihe Rd.
Protein-forward picks from the official specialties list: big fried chicken cutlet, Shilin sausage, Shanghai pan-fried pork buns, herbal-stewed spare ribs.
Street lanes carry the game stalls and clothing; the market building is for sit-down hot food.
tips: Shilin Market B1 food court has ~35 vendors and 600+ seats (steak, xiaolongbao, teppanyaki, oyster omelette) — best base if it rains.
Carry NT$100 notes and coins; some stalls take Taiwanese mobile pay, cards rarely.
Friendly free toilets: Shilin Market and 7-Eleven Wenlin are 24 h.
items.watch: Mostly cash. Weekend and holiday dinner hours are the most crowded. Keep bags in front in dense lanes.

items.title: Back to Via Hotel
items.cost: Taxi from 11 PM: night surcharge +NT$20 per trip (flag fall NT$105 for the first 1.25 km), based on boarding time.
items.getThere: From Jiantan take the Red Line southbound toward Taipei Main Station (same line, no transfer). After 11 PM Red Line trains run every ~12–15 min. Hotel: 台北市中正區重慶南路一段60號.
tips: Leaving E7PLAY at ~11:00 PM, a taxi is quicker than the Orange Line plus a transfer.
